post.title: Why 'It'll Take 10 Minutes' Never Does #shorts
post.description: Leo says his essay will take ten minutes. It's 7 PM. You know how this ends. It's not laziness: almost everyone underestimates. In Roger Buehler, Dale Griffin and Michael Ross's 1994 study (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology), 37 psychology students estimated how long their senior thesis would take: 33.9 days on average. It took 55.5 days. Even their 'if everything goes as poorly as it possibly could' estimate (48.6 days) was too short, and only about 30% finished within their own prediction. Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky named it the planning fallacy (1979): we picture the plan, not the interruptions, and ignore how long similar tasks took last time. Fix: estimate from the last time you did it. Comment 'got me' if your ten minutes became an evening. #psychology #shorts #procrastination #planningfallacy #productivity
